strrev() works at the byte level. For UTF-8 strings, characters can be multi-byte (e.g., Cyrillic characters are 2 bytes each). When you reverse at the byte level, the bytes within each character get swapped, resulting in broken/mojibake output.

Reversed at byte level: 82 D1 B5 D0 B2 D0 B8 D0 80 D1 BF D0 — which is not valid UTF-8 for the reversed word.
